trials.name: IONIS-MAPTRx Phase 1b
trials.primary_endpoint: Number of Participants With Adverse Events That Are Related to Treatment With ISIS 814907
trials.results_summary: The phase 1b trial showed that BIIB080 (MAPT Rx) was well-tolerated with mostly mild-to-moderate adverse events. It led to dose-dependent, sustained reductions in CSF total tau and p-tau181 concentrations. Exploratory findings noted a slightly greater increase in ventricular volume in treatment groups compared to placebo.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence for MAPT Rx (diranersen/BIIB080) as a tau-lowering therapy is grounded in the completed Phase 1b study (NCT03186989), which robustly demonstrated safety and dose-dependent reductions in CSF tau biomarkers (t-tau and p-tau181). These biomarker reductions offer strong proof-of-concept for target engagement via antisense-mediated suppression of tau synthesis in the CNS. A larger Phase 2 trial (CELIA / NCT05399888) is evaluating clinical efficacy (measured by CDR-SB) and longer-term safety in patients with mild cognitive impairment or early AD dementia. While the Phase 1b trial noted mild adverse events (primarily post-lumbar puncture headaches) and a slight increase in ventricular volume requiring further longitudinal monitoring, the drug program remains active with no major clinical safety roadblocks reported to date. Overall, the evidence for target engagement is strong, but evidence for clinical efficacy is pending the Phase 2 readouts following its primary completion in early 2026.
